item.text: {"answer":"2415","solution":"By the Matrix–Tree theorem, the number of spanning trees is the product of the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues divided by 15. For the 3-by-5 grid, these eigenvalues are sums of path-graph eigenvalues: λ_{a,b}=4−2cos(πa/3)−2cos(πb/5), for 0≤a≤2, 0≤b≤4. Omitting (0,0) and multiplying the remaining 14 values gives 15·2415, so the tree count is 2415.","insight":"The Laplacian spectrum of a rectangular grid is obtained by adding the spectra of its two path factors.","insight_justification":"The grid Laplacian is the Kronecker sum of the path Laplacians, so tensor products of path eigenvectors are eigenvectors with eigenvalues equal to the corresponding sums."}
